description: Report one monitor's uptime for each UTC day, oldest first and ending today, to find the day an outage or degradation began. Each day has date, uptime_percentage, downtime_seconds, observed_seconds, degraded_seconds, total_checks, up_checks, down_checks, degraded_checks and maintenance_checks. degraded_seconds is the day's time in confirmed DEGRADED status (an ongoing degradation counts up to now; 0 for days before this monitor's status history began, when the status ledger shipped); it does not lower uptime_percentage. A day with degraded_seconds above 0 and no confirmed outage is a degraded (yellow) day in the dashboard; degraded_checks alone does not make one. uptime_percentage is the share of the day's observed time outside confirmed outages (an outage counts from the first failing probe to the first probe that is not DOWN; a failure only one region saw does not count; maintenance counts as up; hours with no checks are left out); a day with no checks and no outage has a null uptime_percentage, not 100. The check counts are informational: a failed check outside a confirmed outage does not lower uptime_percentage. For 24h, 7d and 30d totals use get_uptime_summary. Returns monitor_id and days.

days.description: How many days to return, 1 to 365; default 30. Capped at the plan's limits.history_retention_days (get_plan_usage), so fewer days can come back.

monitor_id.description: The monitor's uuid from list_monitors. An id that is not a monitor of this organization, or a deleted one, is a 404.

name: get_uptime_daily

degraded_seconds.description: Seconds of this UTC day the monitor spent in confirmed DEGRADED status (from the monitor's status history; an ongoing degradation counts up to now). Maintenance is not subtracted. Zero for days before this monitor's status history began (when the status ledger shipped).

downtime_seconds.description: Seconds of confirmed downtime inside the day.

observed_seconds.description: Seconds of the day the monitor was observed; uptime is measured over this time. Never less than downtime_seconds; 0 means no data.

title: Get a monitor's daily uptime
